predecessors.name: Brythons (Celtic Britons)
predecessors.text: Cliopatria's Brycheiniog shape, the Usk and upper Wye country of south Powys: the page says it 'later formed the southern and larger part of the historic county of Brecknockshire'

successors.name: Lordship of Brecon
successors.text: 'The lands of Brycheiniog became Bernard's Lordship of Brecknock' after 1093; the infobox names 'Lordship of Brecon'

ledger.x: c. 450: Brychan founds Brycheiniog. 'Founded by Brychan Brycheiniog: c.450' after 'Roman Britain'; the text says it was 'probably founded by Irish raiders in the late fifth century' and 'Traditionally, it was founded by and named after a legendary Hiberno-Welsh prince named Brychan'. 1056: Brycheiniog disappears into Gruffydd ap Llywelyn's Wales.
5 August 1063: Gruffydd ap Llywelyn dies and Wales divides.
1072: two border cells pass to Norman England in Cliopatria.
April 1093: Rhys ap Tewdwr falls at Brecon and the conquest is 'mostly finished by Eastertide 1093'.
1093: Brycheiniog becomes the Lordship of Brecknock.
1093: the Welsh kingdom of Brycheiniog ends.

wars.name: Battle of Ffinnant
wars.outcome: The Harleian Chronicle: 'Ithel ap Hywel (king of Gwent) was killed by men from Brycheiniog in the Battle of Ffinnant'; no land changed hands on the page.

wars.name: Norse devastation of Brycheiniog, Gwent and Gwynllwg
wars.outcome: 'in the spring of 896, Brycheiniog, Gwent and Gwynllwg were devastated by the Norsemen'; a raid, no territorial result.

wars.name: Æthelflæd's invasion of Brycheiniog
wars.outcome: 'in the early summer of 916, pushed her advantage by invading Brycheiniog.

wars.name: Gruffydd ap Llywelyn's unification of Wales
wars.outcome: He 'killed his rival Gruffudd ap Rhydderch in battle and recaptured Deheubarth' in 1055, seized Gwent and Morgannwg 'around this time' and ruled all Wales to 5 August 1063; the page does not mention Brycheiniog.

wars.name: Norman conquest of Brycheiniog
wars.outcome: Bernard de Neufmarché's invasion of 1088, Glasbury by autumn 1088, the battle of Brecon in April 1093 where Rhys ap Tewdwr was killed, the Lordship of Brecon; a Welsh revolt from spring 1094 retakes the province in 1095 before Glamorgan expeditions relieve…
